modules.note: Owns logical Endpoint identity, descriptor, capability/resource attachment and endpoint lifecycle; E1 registry is implemented. Does not own routes, transport or Work ledger
Fixed CLI execution and local browser handles; no provider resource ledger or daemon ownership

User-facing agentteams init/start/status/work/stop facade; init delegates v3 bootstrap to initializeLocalConfig and lifecycle delegates to the compiled runtime local launcher. It owns no TLS, child projection, capability implementation or network truth. Candidate evidence: c3c2e0e; U2 continuation: docs/evidence/776fcad-u2-config-impl-20261003/. The ACP `--serve <opencode|dsh> --ip --port` entry is delivered here: cli/agentteams.mjs parses the flags and dispatches to runtime/acp-serve.ts, which starts one daemon plus one engine child with the OpenCode or DSH adapter selected by runtime/acp-serve.ts engineAdapterFor. No compile-only placeholder exists. D04 adds the `agentteams registry start|status|stop --config <file> [--generation <n>]` verbs; they delegate lifecycle truth to runtime/registry-process.ts and start no other daemon.

Owns the source-level local Work Unix socket seam only: typed decode/encode, listener admission, peer drain and own-socket cleanup, plus the single failed or unconfirmed Work receipt projection from a typed frame. It is not the CLI facade, receiver dispatch, config internal owner, or installed runtime.
Owns the single staged package producer, base asset/CLI smoke, installed lifecycle restart smoke, and lifecycle receipt binding. Final SDK runner/graph inclusion remains a D3/U4 input dependency.

Owns link configuration, transport, health and route execution. D04 adds `network/registration-client.ts` as the client transport/health owner for registry registration: it connects the config-selected discovery endpoint over wss, registers, renews the presence lease with a heartbeat, reconnects with bounded backoff on the same endpoint and keeps the original error instead of switching servers. It imports no `config/**`; the config-selected discovery plan and the AgentDeclaration stay in runtime. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. D05 adds the connection layer: `network/teams-negotiation.ts` (the frozen-frame negotiation state machine and the only source of an agreement), `network/teams-session.ts` (one authenticated connection bridged to the injected AcpHost, with locally allocated refs and generation/engine rewrite at the receive boundary), `network/teams-connection-history.ts` (typed kind=connection history over the injected store) and `network/teams-membership.ts` (the per-remote-agent connection/role view assembled from the directory, route and registration surfaces). D05 also adds the additive `RegistrationClient.publish` surface that carries the daemon's real listener route plus its ACP capability over the same D04 path. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network. The D05 closure adds two modules to this owner: `network/teams-ingress.ts` owns the one inbound Teams connection lifecycle on an already authenticated direct-WSS connection, runs the responder negotiation, allocates this side's own transport-scoped connectionId/channelId before any host call so the peer wire ref never reaches the AcpHost, creates the Teams session, and records the typed connection.negotiated / channel.opened / channel.closed / connection.failed facts; `network/teams-status.ts` owns the read-only `TeamsStatusPort` that projects the live connection ledger through projectTeamsMembership and reads the durable connection history, which is the D06 read handoff and stores no state of its own. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network, which now also runs network/teams-ingress.spec.ts, network/teams-status.spec.ts and packages/shared/src/teams-connection.spec.ts. L9 adds `network/teams-egress.ts` to this owner: it is the outbound initiator counterpart of `network/teams-ingress.ts` on an already authenticated direct-WSS connection. It runs the initiator negotiation, records connection.negotiated / connection.failed, observes channel lifecycle with local refs only, and opens the one ACP channel through createTeamsSession.open() so the handshake, the inbound mapping, the delivery pump and the release rules keep their single owner. It reuses createTeamsFrameTransport and TeamsConnectionLedger from the ingress owner, declares no second envelope and never sends acp.open_ack. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network, which now also runs network/teams-egress.spec.ts. L9 command-side adds this module's one production caller in the runtime owner (`runtime/serve-egress.ts`), so the network module itself is unchanged and declares no dial path of its own.

Canonical owner of the Console observation wire contract. BB09 round 12 adds the optional capabilityDetails declaration summary to the shared runtime|directory Agent row fields, its closed parser validation (existing string and capacity/unit checks; illegal shapes rejected, never stripped) and the single declaration-to-summary helper reused by the runtime and Console-hub producers. D00 adds the public ACP envelope and single fault carrier (acp.ts), the type-only engine adapter port (engine.ts), the Teams negotiation frames and the connection-state/history DTOs (teams-connection.ts, teams-state.ts); declarations and parsers only; when this note was written transport, negotiation and history reads were pending D01/D05/D06. 2026-10-14 correction: D01, D05 and D06 now implement those in their own modules, so this module still owns declarations and parsers only. Modular monorepo move (2026-10-23): the former control-protocol/** tree is now packages/shared/src/**; this module owns the shared protocol, wire, codec and DTO library for every consumer, and the runtime still resolves it through the flat tsconfig.runtime.json compile instead of a bare package specifier.

Owner of the DAGpipe Work orchestration slice moved out of runtime/ in the modular monorepo batch: packages/dagpipe/src/{host,protocol}.ts, the checked-in Rust runner source, the build entry build.mjs and the fixture runners. The Node host owns only per-execution AgentWorkClient channels and typed host.call dispatch; it never re-runs, reorders or reconstructs a graph. runtime/dagpipe-work.spec.ts stays a runtime consumer. Gate: teams-dagpipe-runner-build.

Owns Session, RPC/callback correlation, execution admission, permission decisions and execution history semantics. agent-host/acp-host.ts preserves explicit Session ownership, applies D00 policy before engine writes, appends history before effects, distinguishes cancel.requested from the terminal result, and reports RESULT_UNKNOWN on engine exit or channel close. pendingPermissions() exposes each live callback with its controller-visible id and real option set; channelForSession() resolves the owning channel; openedSessions() skips closed channels. projectPermissionOptions and adjudicatePermissionReply accept only engine-offered options and never auto-approve. 2026-10-28 P0 adds sessionEvents(): ordered Console events derived from real ACP frames for user/assistant text parts, tool state, pending/resolved permissions with stable messageIds and engine options, and completed/failed finals. The buffer is cleared with its owning channel and is not a second engine transcript source. Real process and Chrome evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs. Gates: teams-acp-d01-host, teams-acp-d06-control, teams-acp-l9-session-write-side.

Owns the optional, non-permanent Console observation/configuration transport: the authenticated HTTP/SSE surface, the frozen Console API dispatch, and the static UI/API server. Delivered as `console-host/` (`@deepseek-ai/teams-console-host`): `src/auth.ts` (exact-credential Basic auth plus the cross-site guard), `src/server.ts` (static root, extension allowlist and realpath containment for `/ui/`), and `src/http-api.ts` (typed refusals, SSE snapshots, close on owner loss), while the frozen Console API DTO/wire contract it dispatches is the shared library module `packages/shared/src/console-api.ts`. `runtime/control-process.ts:31-32` imports `createConsoleAuthorization`/`createConsoleServer` from `console-host/`, and its line 35 imports the wire parser from that shared module, so D06 and D07 run on this pair. Status is partial, not implemented: there is no published-release evidence, and no installed-copy evidence for the console host outside a control daemon. 2026-10-14 correction (L11): the installed console host now serves the frozen console to a real browser from an installed npm package — docs/evidence/acp-l11-installed-browser-20261014/ (18 checks, exit 0) shows the document and all 18 /ui/ modules byte-identical to the installed package's files, rendered by real Chrome. The D08 acceptance run also exercises it through the installed tarball's control entrypoint. This entry previously read `status: design` with no note, which contradicted both the delivered code and `function-map.json`, where `independent_console_http_server` and `console_v1_http_transport` already name `master-host` as owner. Corrected here; the ownership itself was already right and is unchanged. Gate: teams-acp-d06-control.

Owner of the engine-independent stdio ACP transport between an engine child and agent-host. D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements `acp-adapter/stdio.ts` as the newline-delimited JSON `AcpDuplex` over the frozen `packages/shared/src/engine.ts` port, with CRLF tolerance, a maxFrameBytes bound, typed transport faults and clean-EOF settlement; `acp-adapter/test-peer.mjs` is a labeled test peer, not an engine. The directory exists now. Status is partial, not implemented: the D03 DSH adapter and the D02 OpenCode adapter each compile a real `EngineLaunchSpec` (see the dsh-adapter and opencode-adapter modules), and runtime/acp-serve.ts dispatches both engine kinds over this one transport; installed-copy engine inference is still not proven here. Gate: teams-acp-d01-host.

Owner of the DSH engine adapter: it derives the real DSH native profile patch from the accepted Teams config, compiles the single `EngineLaunchSpec` for the `dsh` kind, and reads the real `initialize`/`session/new` results back as an effectiveness proof. D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b, merged here) implements `dsh-adapter/index.ts` and `dsh-adapter/native-config.ts` with 31 focused specs, and `dsh-adapter/real-engine-evidence.mjs` is committed evidence tooling that drove the real installed DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 through the real D01 runtime for 18/18 gates. It reuses the frozen `packages/shared/src/engine.ts` port, the D00 config/policy owners and the D01 runtime; it adds no second Session path, stdio transport or config source. The `--serve dsh` wiring delivered by this candidate composes it through `runtime/acp-serve.ts` `engineAdapterFor` with the same daemon/host/stdio/readiness/stop code as `--serve opencode`, and the entry removes the owned DSH home on stop and on a failed start. It also declares its own `enforceablePolicies`, derived from `dshHasPolicyEnforcementOwner` over its declared surface, so the blacklist classes the D01 host really enforces (including `capability:` and `client-capability:` keys) are accepted while a key with no enforcement owner is still refused, and the runtime never substitutes `declaredMethods`. Status stays partial, not implemented: the DSH black-box evidence is a live local run against one provider route rather than an installed-copy receipt, the AppSDK compile/verify gate is blocked by the pre-existing 0.1.0014 pin mismatch, and `resource_link` prompts stay refused while the real DSH initialize advertises `embeddedContext: false`. Gate: teams-acp-d03-dsh.

Owns config intent, provider/catalog/model and policy compilation through config/daemon-intent.ts and config/acp-policy.ts. config/relations-intent-store.ts owns the one durable desired-relations record. config/session-intent-store.ts owns the durable Session-write event record and reader watermark, one record per target agent at <home>/.agentteams/sessions/<accountId>/<scopeId>/<agentId>/session-intent.json. 2026-10-28 P0 adds session.create with no invented Session id and no command-time engine result, while session.open remains a control read of the target observation. config/session-observation-store.ts owns the sibling observation record and now validates engine permission options and ordered Console sessionEvents through the frozen Console parsers, with every event restricted to a Session in the same snapshot. config/durable-record.ts remains the one atomic write discipline shared by these stores. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs.

Owns Relay link admission/lifetime and closeGrant revocation. 4e04166 is bound to docs/design/teams-relay-link-lifetime.md and docs/design/dagpipe/graphs/relay-link.graph.json under required teams-relay-link-topology. Static governance bindings are not Work SDK Operators. The opened pair continues after the admission deadline while original controls/generations stay current; server/relay.spec.ts covers the public TLS/WSS behavior. D04 adds the server-owned presence lease in server/relay.ts (DEFAULT_PEER_TTL_MS 90s, one unref'd sweep timer, offline publication that keeps the entry/declaration/generation as history) and server/registry-intent.ts as the single mapping site from the frozen RegistryDaemonIntent to RelayServerOptions, including the explicit TLS_REQUIRED refusal and credential loading. The group surface the registry composes is addressed inside one account and scope (RelayServerOptions.groupScope, required with groupHub): a hub push resolves an exact identity key, group frames from another scope are refused, and server/relay-group.spec.ts proves the same agent id in another account receives neither. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. Public deployment remains deferred.

Owns the AgentTeams runtime lifecycle and transport composition. runtime/acp-serve.ts starts one agent daemon plus one OpenCode or DSH engine child, serves the declared local and authenticated LAN channels, verifies readiness from the engine's session/new response, and stops by explicit PID. runtime/registry-process.ts and runtime/registry-registration.ts own registry lifecycle and discovery publication. runtime/serve-egress.ts owns declared egress rows, while createRelationsIntentWatch reconciles the durable desired-relations record without a control-to-agent channel. Per-dataDirectory single start uses agent-serve-state.lock and retained-engine ownership. 2026-10-28 P0 adds session.create on the managed readiness channel, drains that channel, maps { text } to ACP text blocks while preserving arrays, and publishes ordered sessionEvents plus real permission options. runtime/control-process.ts writes create intents, validates session.open against the target observation, and projects an observed live peer as runtime/sessionCapable with sessionEvents. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs (51/51 r4 final, real control, OpenCode-backed agent and Chrome; r1 40/40 remains history only). No installed-copy, restart, deployed-entrypoint, cross-device or mobile claim is added.

The OpenCode engine adapter (D02, merged candidate 1d4df3a, fixed 1af8fe5/9436aae) is the single compiler of an OpenCode EngineLaunchSpec: compileLaunch derives the managed OpenCode config and its credential env refs from the accepted config, verifyEffective reports the model the engine itself returned from session/new, and declaredMethods/enforceablePolicies declare the adapter capability. runtime/acp-serve.ts is its only production caller. Gate teams-acp-d02-opencode stays partial because the real-engine command needs an installed opencode plus a local stub provider and is not installed-copy evidence.

Owns the four ui/teams-console pages and renders declaration details, discovery, networking, interaction and history from owner projection data with safe text DOM and locale handling. Permission choices come only from engine sessionEvents[].options, refused writes surface typed errors, and Session drafts/page/focus persist across refreshes. The T4 session loop remains delivered: Create Session, selectable Sessions, enabled controlled composer, live timeline and permission buttons. 2026-10-28 P0 adds the only integration correction in this batch: the API client accepts the control daemon's closed session.create durable receipt { acceptedRevision } as well as the direct-owner SessionCreateResult, without weakening either parser. Source-tree real Chrome evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs passed 51/51 (r4 final); the r1 40/40 run remains history only. No mobile claim is made.
